note: trailing decimal point still parses as float
the percent sign is dropped by the character filter, never divided by 100
the comma is dropped by the character filter, never read as a decimal separator
non-numeric characters are dropped, not treated as separators
'e' is not in the filter set: adding exponent support here silently turns 13 into 1000
the dropped 'e' leaves its digits behind rather than an exponent
'+' is not in the filter set, unlike '-'
whitespace is dropped, not treated as a separator
two decimal points is not a float
an interior sign is not a valid int
i64::MAX + 1 saturates via the f64 fallback cast
